agents.name: Scan a website for accessibility issues
agents.description: Use this when the user wants a public website or web page checked for accessibility (WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA, ADA, EAA, Section 508): it loads the live page in a real browser, runs axe-core on it and up to two more same-site pages, and returns a 0-100 score, a letter grade and the failing rules with example elements. Takes 15-40 seconds. Do not use it for pages that need a login, for localhost or private-network addresses, or for pasted HTML.
reasons: This tool scans a public website for WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA accessibility issues, providing a score, grade, and failing rules with example elements.
uncertainties: Execution requires a fresh readiness check.

agents.name: accessibility_audit
agents.description: Run a WCAG accessibility audit on a page using axe-core in a real browser, and report the violations with the elements responsible. Because it runs against a genuinely rendered page, colour-contrast and other rules that depend on layout and computed colour actually fire — these are silently skipped by audits that parse HTML without a layout engine. Use this to check a page meets WCAG before shipping.
reasons: This tool runs a WCAG accessibility audit on a page using axe-core in a real browser, reporting violations with responsible elements.
uncertainties: Execution requires a fresh readiness check.

assessment.explanation: I found several tools that can audit a website for WCAG accessibility issues. These tools can scan live web pages or raw HTML for violations, providing scores, grades, and detailed findings. Some options include scanning a public website for WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA issues, running a WCAG audit with axe-core in a real browser, or performing a quick WCAG-oriented scan of a page's markup.
